subject: Renewal: Term restructure and ephemeral burst ops proposal
messages:
From: Ava Patel <ava.patel@acmeai.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 1 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal + capacity: need additional reserved GPUs + burst behavior

Hi Priyom —

Our renewal window is coming up (end of August) and ops wants to lock in additional reserved capacity. Current summary: baseline committed pool = 32 A100s, peak sustained demand last quarter hit ~48 A100s for a few minutes several times/day.

Questions from our side:
- Can we add a 16-GPU reserved pool to the renewal and have an explicit throughput SLA (p50 p99 latency targets)?
- When we exceed reserved capacity, can overflow be sent to on-demand with per-token pricing, or do you require a hard cap? We need predictable cost behavior — a hard cap that drops requests is risky.
- Any way to tier overflow (first 8 GPUs on cheap on-demand, next 8 on premium on-demand)?

Attaching a usage snapshot and their internal request doc. Please loop legal/procurement as needed.

Thanks,
Ava Patel
Head of Platform Engineering — AcmeAI

---

From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: Ava Patel <ava.patel@acmeai.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal + capacity: need additional reserved GPUs + burst behavior

Hi Ava — thanks for the clarity and the snapshot. High level options we recommend for your renewal: 

1) Committed augmentation + soft spill: add 16 reserved A100-equivalent GPUs (pooled). We'll include a throughput SLO targeting 95th percentile token latency across the pool and an explicit p99 tail objective scoped by request size (<= 1024 tokens).

2) Overflow as on-demand (preferred): soft spill to our on-demand fleet when the reserved pool is saturated. On-demand billing applies for overflow tokens; we'll set a burst pricing tier and a per-minute cap to avoid runaway spend.

3) Tiered overflow (custom): we can route the first 8 overflow GPUs to our lower-cost spot-equivalent nodes and the next 8 to higher-reliability on-demand nodes. This requires a short ops lead time (2-3 weeks) to configure routing policies.

Attached: a draft amendment with the 16-GPU add-on and proposed SLO language. Ben has suggested a conservative p99 target in the doc.

Next steps: if this matches what you need, Marissa will send commercial terms and Jordan (legal) can review the overflow language. Happy to hop on a 30-min call tomorrow.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Senior Sales — Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai

Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal + capacity: need additional reserved GPUs + burst behavior

Ava — quick technical notes on the SLOs and routing: 

- For your workload (mixture of chat + long generation), we recommend isolating interactive traffic to a low-latency pool. That lowers p99 substantially.
- Soft spill will preserve request ordering and KV cache continuity for cache hits; completely cold fallbacks will have a one-time warm-up penalty.
- We can implement a routing weight that prefers spot-equivalent nodes for the first layer of overflow; if those nodes are constrained, requests will cascade to on-demand.

Operational guardrails we suggest adding to the amendment:
- Daily spend alert at a configured threshold (we can default to 150% of mean overflow spend month-to-date).
- Auto-throttle policy that gracefully reduces concurrent ephemeral sessions if cost or latency exceeds policy for >10 minutes.

Happy to review the exact latency numbers on a call.

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Ava Patel <ava.patel@acmeai.com>, priyom_das@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal + capacity: need additional reserved GPUs + burst behavior

Ava — commercial framing:

- 16-GPU reserved add-on at a 12-month term: 18% list discount off our reserved rate if signed with the renewal.
- Soft spill to on-demand: +10% markup on list on overflow tokens unless you accept a small commitment to a burst pool (see option B below).
- Option B (Burst pool commitment): commit to a 4-GPU burst reserve at a lower on-demand rate; any overflow beyond that follows the tiered routing and will be billed at the standard overflow tiers. The burst reserve gives you cheaper short-term headroom and caps effective marginal cost for small spikes.

If procurement needs a formal amendment we will attach pricing tables and a one-page churn protection clause (no early-termination fee for traffic above baseline for 60 days post-renewal).

Marissa Cole
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

From: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
To: Ava Patel <ava.patel@acmeai.com>, priyom_das@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal + capacity: need additional reserved GPUs + burst behavior

Ava / team — legal points on overflow:

- We prefer soft spill language that routes to on-demand and invoices overflow usage. A strict hard cap (requests dropped) is operationally risky for our customers and for us — we don't accept hard caps that cause data loss, but we can include optional throttling policies.
- Add an explicit spend protection clause: daily and monthly caps that auto-alert and can trigger an opt-in gating flow (Procurement can approve extra spend mid-month).
- If Acme requires a maximum per-request failure mode, we can offer a short-term SLA credit for specific endpoints instead of a hard drop.

Please let us know procurement's max acceptable daily spend threshold and whether DocuSign execution is acceptable.

Jordan Blake
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference

From: Ava Patel <ava.patel@acmeai.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 5 Aug 2027 15:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal + capacity: need additional reserved GPUs + burst behavior

Thanks all — this is helpful and close to what we discussed. Procurement confirmed they can accept overflow billed at on-demand with the +10% markup, provided we get: 
1) daily spend alerts (set to 200% of baseline overflow by default)
2) an auto-throttle that reduces concurrency for long (>10 min) cost spikes
3) a one-time 30% credit on overflow spend for the first 7 days after go-live to account for expected traffic variability.

We are good to proceed on the 16-GPU add-on + the small 4-GPU burst reserve. Please send the amendment and DocuSign link; procurement will countersign once legal confirms the spend protection language.

Ava
